content: 1. The independence of data extraction was not confirmed. 2. Methods to minimize errors during data extraction were unclear. 3. The methods used to combine studies were deemed appropriate. 4. The likelihood of publication bias was not assessed. 5. Recommendations for policy and/or practice were supported by the reported data. 6. Specific directives for new research were unclear. 7. The overall critical appraisal score for the study was low, with a rating of 2 out of 11. For randomized controlled trials (RCTs), the following observations were made: True randomization was used for assigning participants to treatment groups in both studies reviewed (Coolen et al., 2004, and Kirby et al., 2011). Allocation concealment was not implemented in either study. Treatment groups were similar at baseline in both studies. Blinding of participants and those delivering treatment was not applicable. Outcome assessors were not blinded to treatment assignment in either study. Treatment groups were treated identically, except for the intervention of interest. Follow-up was complete, and differences between groups in follow-up were adequately described and analyzed. Participants were analyzed in the groups to which they were randomized in one study, while this was unclear in the other. Appropriate statistical analysis was used in both studies. The trial design was appropriate, and deviations from standard RCT design were accounted for in both studies. The overall critical appraisal score for RCTs was high (9/11 for one study) and moderate (7/11 for the other). For pre-post studies, the following findings were noted: Temporal relationships between variables were clearly established. Comparisons between participants receiving similar treatments were not applicable. Control groups were not applicable. Follow-up was complete in one study, while this was unclear or not applicable in others. Appropriate statistical analysis was used in some studies, while this was unclear in others. The overall critical appraisal score for pre-post studies ranged from low to high, depending on the study. For cross-sectional studies, the following observations were made: Inclusion criteria for the sample were clearly defined. Study subjects and settings were described in detail. Confounding factors were not identified or addressed. Appropriate statistical analysis was used in both studies. The overall critical appraisal score for cross-sectional studies was moderate. For qualitative studies, the following findings were noted: Congruity between the stated philosophical perspective and research methodology was unclear in one study but present in another. Congruity between research methodology and research questions, data collection methods, data analysis, and interpretation of results was present in both studies. Statements locating the researcher culturally or theoretically were absent. The influence of the researcher on the research and vice versa was not addressed. Participants and their voices were adequately represented. Ethical considerations were met, and evidence of ethical approval was provided. Conclusions drawn from the research flowed logically from the data analysis. Excluded studies were identified for various reasons, including lack of relevant information on wheelchair services, absence of specific findings for wheelchair users, or overlapping data with other studies.
